item.title: Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked
item.description: Homicide rates are falling across much of the world, but organised crime is on the rise in many regions as criminal networks diversify into trafficking, migrant smuggling, and the exploitation of natural resources, a new UN report launched on Wednesday revealed.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Countries adopt global blueprint to tackle fast-evolving crime in digital age
item.description: Countries adopted on Saturday a new global blueprint for tackling rapidly evolving forms of crime, as the UN’s largest gathering on crime prevention and criminal justice opened in Abu Dhabi with a call for stronger international cooperation.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN Crime Congress: Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it
item.description: Sitting in her Vienna office ahead of a pivotal UN gathering in Abu Dhabi, Monica Juma is focused on a simple reality: crime has evolved faster than many of the institutions designed to combat it.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors mark 9/11 with counter-terrorism push on AI and drones
item.description: The Security Council met to mark 25 years since the 9/11 attacks with a briefing on counter-terrorism as ambassadors take stock of a threat that has morphed dramatically since resolution 1373 built the council's counter-terrorism machinery in 2001. Briefers highlighted militants' growing use of artificial intelligence, drones and encrypted platforms for recruitment and attack planning.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Advance safety for all’: International police cooperation helps tackle cross-border crime
item.description: As criminal networks increasingly exploit weak institutions and operate across borders, the UN says no police force can tackle them alone.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: One in five children in 21 nations faced tech-facilitated sexual abuse: UNICEF
item.description: About 20 million children aged 12 to 17 – one in five across 21 countries – were sexually exploited by perpetrators using technology such as social media, according to a UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) report released on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti ramps up the fight against gangs in the capital, but violence spreads elsewhere
item.description: The killings in Kenscoff began late Sunday, when armed men descended on the farming community in the hills overlooking Haiti’s capital, setting homes ablaze and attacking residents. By Monday, bodies lay in the streets and survivors were searching for missing relatives.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Breaking the silence over sexual violence against men and boys in war
item.description: Conflicts can expose civilians and detainees to grave abuses; the challenge is not only to document these crimes, but also to ensure all survivors are recognised, protected and able to access justice and care.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: International Criminal Court: New US sanctions ‘a flagrant attack’ against its independence
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday responded to a new round of US sanctions targeting its president and a senior prosecutor, calling them “a flagrant attack” against the court.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Zambia: Arrests and detention of political opponents following election raises concern
item.description: In the wake of President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia’s re-election for a second five-year term, UN human rights chief has raised concerns over the reported arrests and detention of political opponents in the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Singapore: Independent rights experts urge immediate end to ‘unlawful use’ of death penalty
item.description: Independent UN Human Rights Council-appointed experts on Tuesday condemned the execution of at least 16 people in Singapore for drug-related offences this year and urged the country to end its “continued and unlawful use of capital punishment.”
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Meth trafficking across Middle East becoming more advanced, UNODC warns
item.description: Authorities in Iran intercepted 3,663 kilogrammes of methamphetamines headed for Europe and the Persian Gulf in the first quarter of 2026, according to the UN’s drugs and crime fighting agency (UNODC).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Afghanistan: UN tells Taliban to open up on abuses committed by security forces
item.description: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghans still have almost no way of knowing whether soldiers, police and morality officers who abuse their power ever face consequences – and that secrecy is corroding trust in the State, the UN said Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Trapped by a Facebook job advert, freed by a stranger in a taxi
item.description: Sofia* was 27, raising her seven-year-old son alone in Venezuela, and running out of options. For years she had distributed personal hygiene products door to door, but as her customers’ finances collapsed, so did her income.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Returning Afghans face growing risk of trafficking as crises deepen
item.description: Afghans returning from neighbouring countries are facing growing risks of human trafficking and exploitation as overlapping humanitarian and economic crises leave many struggling to survive, the UN warned on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Forced online scams: IOM warns trafficking networks are booming
item.description: A job advert can hide a criminal network, and a single click can lead to a nightmare. Hundreds of thousands of people are trafficked every year on the promise of legitimate work abroad, only to be held captive and forced into online scam operations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Judges should be superhuman’: The invisible burden behind the bench
item.description: When conflict erupts, disasters strike or political crises unfold, courts are among the few institutions expected to keep functioning – ensuring the essential rule of law is maintained.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: International Criminal Court Prosecutor Karim Khan dismissed
item.description: Member States of the International Criminal Court dismissed its Prosecutor Karim Khan following disciplinary proceedings related to widely reported sexual misconduct allegations at an emergency session at UN Headquarters in New York on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Business as usual is a business of death’: UN adopts road safety pledge over US objection
item.description: The UN General Assembly closed its first ever High-level Meeting on road safety on Tuesday by adopting a sweeping new declaration aimed at halving road deaths by 2030 – over the sole objection of the United States.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Sexual violence in DR Congo, deaths in Ukraine and Russia, crime in Southeast Asia
item.description: Independent UN human rights experts on Tuesday condemned the M23 armed group’s “reign of terror” over territory it controls in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), calling for an end to the Rwanda-backed group’s sexual torture and violence against civilians.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: Signs of hope despite gang violence and political uncertainty
item.description: For millions of Haitians, daily life has become a struggle to stay safe, find enough food and simply move around their own neighbourhood.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Baristas behind bars: Thai prisoners brew a path back to daily life
item.description: It looks like a regular coffee shop, albeit set up in an old red bus. Stairs lead up to a serving hatch, with a menu of drink options. A selection of jaunty coffee-related messages like “My one and only love: Americano” and “Miss you a latte,” adorn the side of the bus.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: Training the next generation to fight corruption
item.description: How do you tackle corruption in a country grappling with insecurity, weak institutions and widespread impunity? In Haiti, the Government and the United Nations are betting on the country's youth.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: West Africa and the Sahel: Terrorism is changing its face
item.description: Jihadist groups are no longer content with launching attacks in West Africa and the Sahel: they administer territories, control trade routes, exploit new technologies and are gradually pushing their influence all the way to the Gulf of Guinea.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: International Criminal Court ‘a critical cog’ in global justice efforts
item.description: The United Nations upheld the critical role of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Monday in the global fight to end impunity for grave crimes amid calls for it to be abolished.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As deadly as war and as powerful as governments, global organized crime remains in the shadows
item.description: When people think of the world’s deadliest threats, armed conflicts usually come to mind first. Yet every year, organized crime quietly claims a comparable number of lives.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Global drug use reaches record high as increasingly potent synthetic drugs spread
item.description: More people are using drugs than ever before, while synthetic substances are reshaping illicit markets and exposing vulnerable communities to greater health risks, according to the UN World Drug Report 2026, released on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Monica Juma: Steering global cooperation at a time of converging threats
item.description: Criminal networks are moving faster, reaching further and blurring the lines between threats. Into this shifting landscape steps Monica Juma, taking on one of the UN’s most demanding security and justice portfolios.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council weighs future of UN war crimes mechanism as closure nears
item.description: The Security Council on Friday weighed the future of the UN mechanism responsible for completing the remaining work of the international tribunals for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia, as members debated how to preserve its legacy while bringing its mandate to an orderly close.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: UN rights office welcomes new judicial units to tackle gang violence and impunity
item.description: The UN human rights office, OHCHR, on Tuesday welcomed the opening of two specialised judicial units in Haiti, saying the move marked “a significant step toward tackling widespread impunity in the country.”
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
